reden: Yes. The report explicitly identifies the same tipping-based attack: the fulfiller can append extra ERC20 consideration items (tips), Create._processBaseOrderConsideration accepts them, and later PaymentEscrow._settlePayment attempts to transfer that ERC20, which if malicious (reverting) causes stopRent to revert permanently, locking the NFT and escrowed funds. This is described twice in the report ([High] “Renter adds malicious ERC20 tip …” and [High] “Seaport tip items let the renter inject an attacker ERC20 …”), matching the vulnerability’s mechanism, code path (Create._processBaseOrderConsideration and PaymentEscrow._settlePayment), impact, and fix direction (disallow tips/whitelist tokens).
